fields.outcome: A developer can start a deterministic local web application and provide an authorized test account that later AutoTour stories can exercise safely.
fields.scope: Create a minimal fixture application with login, a protected profile journey, stable semantic controls, deterministic routes, and observable profile API calls. Exclude AutoTour capture, annotation, dependency mapping, and production authentication patterns.
fields.acceptance: The fixture starts locally, enforces test authentication, exposes the agreed profile journey, and passes automated browser-level behavior checks without committing credentials.
fields.decisions: Own files under fixtures/demo-app and tests dedicated to the fixture. Contract routes are /login and /settings/profile; observed endpoints are POST /api/login, GET /api/profile, and PUT /api/profile. Credentials come from AUTOTOUR_USERNAME and AUTOTOUR_PASSWORD with documented test-only defaults.
fields.verification: Start the fixture on an available local port, verify its health endpoint, exercise failed and successful login, update the profile, and confirm the expected API traffic and persisted in-memory result.
fields.dependencies: Node.js 20 or newer and the repository Playwright dependency.
fields.risks: An overbuilt fixture would distract from AutoTour; implicit credentials or unstable selectors would weaken later evidence.

criteria.expectation: A documented command starts the fixture on a configurable local port and exposes a health endpoint.
Invalid credentials are rejected and environment-provided test credentials create an authenticated session.
An authenticated user can open profile settings, change a display name, save it, and observe the saved value.
The fixture exposes the agreed routes, semantic labels, and login/profile API endpoints used by later stories.
No password, cookie, token, or browser storage state is committed or printed by tests.
Automated tests cover health, authentication failure, authentication success, and the profile update journey.
